newsitem.title: USA: Maryland Gov. to propose income tax cut - WashPost.
newsitem.headline: Maryland Gov. to propose income tax cut - WashPost.

text.p: Maryland Gov. Parris Glendening will propose a cut in personal income taxes to improve the state's business climate, the Washington Post reported in Tuesday editions, quoting administration sources.
The paper said the Democratic governor may unveil his proposal as early as Tuesday afternoon after briefing state legislative and political leaders in the morning.
It quoted sources familiar with the deliberations as saying they expected the income tax cut to be about 10 percent and to be partially offset by a rise in Maryland's 36-cents-per-pack cigarette tax.
A tax cut would require approval by the state's Democrat-controlled General Assembly, which convenes in January.
Glendening has faced tough pressure by corporate groups and political factions to propose an income tax reduction.
